object.name: evi.baxandall~
object.digest: Emulation of a classic baxandall EQ
object.description: An EQ tone control shape popularised in the 1950s, often used in HiFi equipment and guitar amplifiers. Baxandall is a special EQ as the frequency response is fixed, and depends on the simple high level gain control inputs ('treble' and 'bass').
object.discussion: This is based on the DirectForm II AirWindows plugin, MIT. For similar tone shaping in evieve (all of which are trapezoidal integrated) @see: <o>evi.damp~</o>, <o>evi.damp.macro~</o>, <o>evi.onepole.shelving~</o>, <o>evi.tone.macro~</o>.

inlets.description: Mono or left input depending on @stereo attribute.
Nothing or right input depending on @stereo attribute.

outlets.description: Mono or left output depending on @stereo attribute.
Nothing or right output depending on @stereo attribute.

attributes.name: bass
attributes.description: The amount of bass in the tone. As a baxandall EQ, this also shapes the frequency response, creating a mid frequency notch at high levels. Ultimately 'bass' and 'treble' behave like shelving filters, at opposite extremes creating a tilt-like filter.

attributes.name: smooth
attributes.description: If on, the internal coefficients are lightly smoothed at an optimal part in the DSP chain. If not updating 'treble' and 'bass' dynamically 'smooth' can safely be turned off.

attributes.name: stereo
attributes.description: If @stereo is on, the EQ is stereo input stereo output. If @stereo is off, the EQ is mono in mono out (left in and out).

attributes.name: treble
attributes.description: The amount of treble in the tone. As a baxandall EQ, this also shapes the frequency response, creating a high mid frequency notch at high levels. Ultimately 'bass' and 'treble' behave like shelving filters, at opposite extremes creating a tilt-like filter.
